contexts.text: Spiritual Angels... never draw conclusions about matters of faith from intellectual, rational, and scientific things.
As I could infer from the fact... AC 4329:2.
Jehovah hath restrained me from bearing ().
As may be inferred from the fact...
The conclusion of the thought, or the answer, comes from perception or conscience...
All things which he would afterwards conclude concerning rational truth. Signified.
The state of conclusion concerning rational truth is here treated of.
When he consults scientifics, and forms conclusions from them. Signified.

They looked into everything with me which was [a matter serviceable for forming] a conclusion, from which they formed a conclusion so dexterously concerning the interiors of my thoughts and affections, that I began to be afraid of thinking anything more, for they disclosed things I did not know I had, but which I could not but acknowledge from the conclusions which they made.
When they form conclusions about the truths of faith from their own fallacies...
The internal of the Natural is formed by those things which are analytically and analogically inferred...

He who thinks and forms conclusions from the interior Natural, is rational in proportion as he imbibes through the Rational; but he who thinks and forms conclusions through the exterior Natural, is sensuous in proportion as he imbibes from sensuous things.
By sensuous things being rejected... is meant that the conclusions concerning interior things thence derived are to be rejected. Signified.

Those things which are in the interior Natural are called forth by the Rational, and through these those which are in the exterior Natural; not that the very things which are there are called forth, but those which are inferred or as it were drawn out of them...
What is provided, and thence concluded. Signified.
To lift up the head = to conclude, and in the supreme sense, to provide; for the Divine conclusion and the execution of the thing concluded is Providence. AC 5155. AC 5162.
He shut them up in custody () = separation from himself. To give or shut up in custody = rejection, thus separation.
Intellectual and sensuous things arise by a method of extraction; for intellectual things are inferences, which, when made, are separated, and advance to what is more lofty...
Through [the representation of] Zebulon it here treats of those in the Church who form conclusions about spiritual things from scientifics, and thus strengthen them in themselves...
He shall dwell at the haven of the seas = the life in which there is the conclusion of truth from scientifics.
The wilderness hath shut them in () = that darkness has taken possession of them.
Natural truths, which are conclusions from the objects of the external senses, especially sight...
By this was represented that to act and teach from good is to conclude innumerable things which are of truth, but not contrariwise.
A conclusion concerning the Israelitish nation. Signified.
It is the evil of falsity when man has confirmed evil in himself, and has concluded that it is not evil, and therefore does it...
From which it may be concluded as to the rest.
It may be concluded from this alone... HH 376. HH 390. HH 395:end. HH 415. HH 416:end. HH 435.

It follows that there are three degrees of will and understanding and of conclusion therefrom; for the will is the receptacle of love, the understanding of wisdom, and the thing concluded is the use from these.

When they are opened towards Hell, the reigning love which is of the will gains the highest or inmost place; the thought of falsity which is of the understanding from that love gains the second or middle place; and the conclusion of the love through the thought, or of the will through the understanding, gains the lowest place.
The things concluded from their two degrees, which are either laid up in the memory as knowledges, or determined into acts in the body, make the ultimate degree in the Heavens.
These three things are in every word, because a word is something concluded, having in it sound, articulation, and meaning.
There are a number of things which belong to both love and wisdom; as consent, conclusion, and determination to act...
By this faculty, which is the faculty of interiorly understanding things, and forming conclusions as to what is just and fair, and good and true, man is distinguished from beasts...
The dragon shut up () = that they are altogether removed.
They said, Form a conclusion from these things... CL 134:6. CL 135:end. CL 233:7.
They conclude eggs in which are birds of night...
There are some who do not perceive truth, but conclude it from confirmations through appearances...
From one established principle theorems of the same sort are deduced...
From which comes the conclusion...
The notion that... God the Father included all mankind under a sentence of damnation.
What is there considered, concluded upon, and determined into act...
In a moment man can think and conclude what he cannot express in an hour.
The same may be clearly inferred from this...
The will enters the understanding by the intention, and prompts it to occupy itself with and consider means, and to conclude on such as tend to effects.
That falsities and evils had entered into all things of the Church, is signified by He hath shut up into the hand of the enemy the walls of her palaces ().
He shut up their beast to the hail ().
Reasonings from the spiritual man, which are rather to be called conclusions from reasons and from truths...
I will shut up Egypt in the hand of a hard lord () = that there will reign the evil of falsity.
To shut up the city and its fulness () = to condemn the doctrine because it is full of the falsities of evil, and obsessed by them.
